cohort: 111 mothers who had recently given birth and 1554 maternity-ward staff members at 8 Finnish maternity hospitals
finding: Rooming-in was found to be utilized to a satisfactory extent, especially after vaginal birth, and was regarded as a positive experience by most mothers, but factors like mode of childbirth, parity, and staff training were associated with its implementation.
mod_finding: Rooming-in was used less frequently after cesarean section, and the need for supplementation was higher when rooming-in was not employed.
